speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether an update can be provided on the work of the recently announced Bus Safety Tripartite Taskforce; (b) what are the key areas of focus of the Taskforce; and (c) to what extent has the Taskforce engaged different stakeholders to enhance bus and commuter safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Taskforce also visited all four bus operators to understand their safety practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: During the visits, Taskforce members also had the opportunity to engage face-to-face with bus captains to understand their concerns and challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: To learn from stakeholders outside the bus sector, the Taskforce engaged the Singapore Armed Forces' (SAF’s) Transport Command to learn about safety initiatives for transport operators in the SAF.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Taskforce conveys its thanks to all participants of its surveys, focus group discussions and visits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It is reviewing the feedback and learning points from the numerous engagements.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am particularly interested in this Parliamentary Question (PQ) because of the bus safety issues, following the previous PQs I had asked before, especially the ones a few years ago on the accident near the bus interchange.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And what other new consultations or engagements does he plan to make over the next few months, before the findings are released next year?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This remains the case since the announcement by Minister Chee Hong Tat on the formation of the Taskforce in July 2024.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: But of course, there are always areas that we can look at to enhance these standards.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: As to what further steps we will be taking to get the inputs necessary, as I mentioned in my speech, we will be engaging international experts, overseas regulators as well as operators to identify best practices that we can adopt in the local public bus sector.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have Clementi residents who are ageing and so are understandably giving much attention to whether our bus services, our bus infrastructure continue to be accommodating of the elderly.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Minister of State, in the stakeholder consultations, will there be attention given to engaging healthcare professionals who work with the elderly and may have insights into the challenges faced by the elderly?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Professionals such as geriatricians, physiotherapists, occupational therapists and other allied health professionals with relevant experience.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This is one area we are trying to see how best we can progress.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This is something that we could look at to see how we can bolster the safety for seniors while they travel in our buses.
